title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
authors: T. Valet, J. Li, H. Jaffrès, V. Cros, M. Chshiev, R. Raimondi
abstract: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. However, a new {\em current-gradient-induced} torque emerges in nanoscale geometries. For a series of Ni-based bilayers, the computed Ni thickness dependence of the current-gradient-induced torque is in quantitative agreement with measurements previously attributed to orbital torques. We discuss how this opens a new avenue for the electrical control of magnetic orders, possibly also including the Néel vector of metallic altermagnets.
summary: This paper theoretically predicts that spin-orbit interaction induces transverse spin textures at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnets. These textures give rise to a novel current-gradient-induced Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT). The model successfully reproduces experimental measurements on Ni bilayers, opening a new pathway for electrical control of magnetic order.
main_problem: The paper theoretically establishes the existence of transverse spin textures at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnets and predicts a novel current-gradient-induced Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) arising from these textures.
main_result: A current-gradient-induced SOT is predicted that is distinct from torques associated with broken inversion symmetry, and its magnitude quantitatively agrees with measurements on Ni-based bilayers previously attributed to orbital torques.
method: The work combines theoretical derivations using a two-band model near band intersections with *ab initio* computations (VASP) and solving the semiclassical Boltzmann equation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals (Fe, Co, Ni) and their electronic structure near the Fermi surface, utilizing a two-band model to analyze spin-orbit interaction effects.
key_observables: Transverse spin texture ($s^{\perp}$), current-gradient-induced torque ($	au^E_{	ext{ib}}$), and the damping-like torque efficiency ($\xi_{E	ext{DL}}$).
important_parameters: The thickness ($t$) of the Ni-based bilayers, and the strength of the spin-orbit interaction (SOI).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a two-band theory assuming other bands are energetically distant, and the torque derivation is performed at the leading order in the semiclassical expansion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spin mosaics showing transverse spin textures at Fermi surface seams (Fig. 1, 2), and show current density profiles and the thickness dependence of the damping-like torque efficiency ($\xi_{E	ext{DL}}$) compared to experiments (Fig. 3, 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical origin of transverse spin textures via SOI in centrosymmetric ferromagnets, deriving the current-gradient-induced torque, and finally validating this prediction by comparing the calculated torque dependence on film thickness with experimental measurements on Ni bilayers.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter magnetism, the detailed quantum kinetic theory and the focus on emergent, symmetry-protected torques provide a deep theoretical framework for understanding spin-charge coupling, which is relevant to open quantum systems dynamics.
